title: A failed run, one marked holding, and no completed trade decision

A failed run, one marked holding, and no completed trade decision

Paper trading · 2026-10-22T17:00:09.404222-04:00

At the 2026-10-22 21:00:09 UTC cutoff, the paper account snapshot reports $2,000 cash and equity. The mean-reversion book has $1,950.01 cash and $1,995.90 marked equity, with its MU holding marked from a 20:00 UTC bid/ask midpoint snapshot. The other two books each show $2,000 cash and equity. The day's scheduled run failed during asset validation, and the context contains no completed proposal, deterministic risk approval or rejection, submitted order, broker fill, or simulated fill. The account and book figures are snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed; the MU quote predates the report cutoff.

Today's lesson: Separate failed runs, decisions, and fills

A run failure is not the same as a decision to wait. Today's 19:15 UTC run failed asset validation because nine assets carried the unsupported exchange value TXSE; the supplied records therefore do not establish a completed proposal or risk outcome. Separately, the MU observation is timestamped 20:00 UTC, one hour before the report cutoff. At that snapshot, $939.88 average cost compared with $862.71 observed price gives a $77.17 per-share difference; on 0.053191 shares, that works out to about $4.10 unrealized loss, excluding fees.

How to read the two snapshot times

The MU quote record lists a bid of $818.28 and an ask of $907.13. Their midpoint is $862.705, recorded as $862.71. The holding's $45.89 value and -$4.10 unrealized P/L use that observation at 20:00 UTC. The separate paper account snapshot was captured at 21:00:09 UTC and does not supply paper holding details. Neither timestamp should be treated as a live price.

What to watch next

For the next report, check whether a run completed and whether it recorded a proposal, deterministic risk result, and any actual fill. Keep broker fills distinct from simulated fills, and compare each holding with its own timestamped price observation. The supplied context does not establish what future activity will occur.

Snapshot: A recorded price observation at a particular time. It may be older than the report cutoff and is not necessarily a live or official closing price.

Unrealized P/L: The estimated gain or loss on a holding that has not been realized by a sale. Here it uses the supplied observed price and excludes fees.

Realized P/L: Gain or loss recorded from completed transactions. The mean-reversion book reports $0 realized P/L.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
